dedupe_keys.name: sirius inventory of critical infrastructure and human impacted areas in alaskan permafrost regions

description: SIRIUS (Synthesized Inventory of CRitical Infrastructure and HUman-Impacted Areas in Permafrost Regions of AlaSka) combines infrastructure, land use, permafrost and watershed information for Alaska in one queryable geodatabase. It merges the Sentinel-1/2 derived Arctic coastal human impact dataset (SACHI), OpenStreetMap infrastructure, the ARCADE pan-Arctic catchment database, the modelled northern hemisphere permafrost map of Obu and others (2018) and the Alaska Department of Environmental Conservation contaminated sites database. It was published on 25 September 2023 by researchers at the Alfred Wegener Institute (Kaiser, Boike, Grosse and Langer). The GeoPackages, about 9.5 GB in total with road and rail network layers, and the Python processing scripts are available free on Zenodo under CC BY 4.0. Caveats: infrastructure completeness follows OpenStreetMap and SACHI detection, and permafrost values are modelled at coarse resolution. It supports exposure analysis of roads, pipelines, buildings and contaminated sites to permafrost thaw; a related record is OpenStreetMap, one of its sources.
